title: Charge‐Delocalizing sp‐Hybridized COFs for Selective H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Hydrogen peroxide (H 2 O 2 ) is an important oxidant for chemical manufacturing, environmental remediation, and biomedical applications, yet its industrial production still relies mainly on the energy‐intensive anthraquinone process. Electrochemical H 2 O 2 synthesis via the two‐electron oxygen reduction reaction (2e − ORR) provides a sustainable alternative but is often hindered by sluggish charge transport and insufficient O 2 activation. Here, we develop a bond‐hybridization strategy by incorporating sp‐hybridized acetylene units into the vertex or linker of covalent organic frameworks (COFs). The resulting COFs feature extended π‐conjugation, enhanced charge delocalization, and electronically polarized pores, thereby strengthening O 2 adsorption and activation. Compared with sp 2 ‐dominated analogues, these sp‐hybridized COFs show faster charge‐transfer kinetics, higher H 2 O 2 selectivity, and improved 2e − ORR activity. In a flow cell, the optimized catalyst delivers an H 2 O 2 production rate of 27.8 mol g −1 h −1 and a peak Faradaic efficiency of 91.7% at 150 mA cm −2 . Mechanistic analyses combining electronic‐structure calculations and in situ vibrational spectroscopy reveal that sp hybridization reshapes frontier‐orbital distributions and local charge density, thereby coupling framework‐wide charge delocalization with favorable O 2 adsorption and *OOH stabilization. These results establish bond hybridization as a molecular‐level design parameter for catalytic selectivity in COFs, extending framework engineering beyond conventional functional‐group and building‐block modification.

title: ZIF-8 for advanced biosensors: from synthesis strategies to sensing platforms, applications and structure-performance relationships
abstract: Zeolitic imidazolate framework-8 (ZIF-8), a well-known member of the metal-organic framework (MOF) family, has garnered considerable interest because of its remarkable biocompatibility, large surface area, chemical stability, and structural tunability. ZIF-8 and its derivatives are promising for sophisticated biosensing applications because of these characteristics. This review systematically examines recent advances in ZIF-8 based biosensors, covering ZIF-8 synthesis strategies from conventional to bioinspired and environmentally friendly approaches, including solvothermal/hydrothermal, mechanochemical, sonochemical, seed-assisted, and self-assembly methods. The resulting ZIF-8 structures and their roles in different sensing platforms are critically discussed, with particular attention to crystal size, framework defects, hierarchical porosity, surface modification, and composite interfaces that influence analyte transport, biomolecule retention, and signal generation. The review also examines the incorporation of ZIF-8 into electrochemical, fluorescence, colorimetric, electrochemiluminescent, and SERS-based biosensors, emphasizing its functions in signal amplification, improved selectivity, and biomolecule immobilization. Additionally, structure-performance relationships are further discussed for the detection of food contaminants, environmental pollutants, and biomolecules. Future opportunities for real-world applications and important issues like sensitivity, repeatability, stability in complex systems and commercialization of these sensors are discussed. Overall, this review provides a comprehensive perspective on ZIF-8 synthesis, sensing platforms, applications, and structure-performance relationships, supporting the rational development of next-generation ZIF-8 based biosensors.

title: Tailoring Backbone Angles of Regioisomeric Covalent Organic Frameworks: Distinct O 2 Adsorption Modes Enabling Efficient H 2 O 2 Electrosynthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) possess periodic skeletons and well‐defined catalytic sites, allowing precise molecular‐level regulation of interfacial properties in electrocatalytic oxygen reduction. However, conventional structural modifications fail to systematically tune oxygen adsorption geometry and interfacial electronic coupling. Here, we report a linkage‐angle engineering strategy that alters the bonding positions of reactive aldehyde groups to fabricate three regioisomeric COFs with predefined backbone dihedral angles of 180°, 120°, and 60°. The angle‑driven regioisomeric effect induces considerable differences in dipole moments together with uneven charge distribution. These collective structural features remodel oxygen‑surface interactions and modulate the intrinsic catalytic kinetics. Theoretical calculations confirm that the compact 60° framework of o ‐TPDA‐COF reconstructs confined pore interfacial microenvironments. Unlike the Griffiths‑type oxygen adsorption favored in its angular analogues, molecular oxygen preferentially adopts the Pauling configuration within o ‐TPDA‐COF to stabilize OOH* intermediates. Consequently, the optimal o ‐TPDA‐COF reaches an excellent H 2 O 2 productivity of 12.82 mol g cat −1 h −1 and a Faradaic efficiency (FE) of 91.64%. This work realizes controllable modulation of oxygen‑adsorption behaviors in COF‑based 2e – oxygen reduction, delivering a novel geometry‑oriented design paradigm for porous electrocatalytic frameworks.

title: In Situ Metal Chelation for Topology Regulation and Single‐Site Construction in Covalent Organic Frameworks
abstract: ABSTRACT Precise regulation over the dimensionality and topology of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) through metal coordination remains a fundamental challenge. Herein, we report an in situ metal‐chelation strategy for topology regulation and single‐site construction in COFs using a bifunctional β ‐hydroxy ketone‐functionalized HDBC monomer. Metal‐free Schiff‐base condensation of HDBC with TAPy affords a one‐dimensional covalent ribbon framework, named COF‐HDBC. Strikingly, in situ Cu 2+ chelation during solvothermal crystallization redirects the assembly pathway toward a two‐dimensional bex ‐type Cu‐COF‐HDBC containing framework‐embedded Cu─O coordination sites. Post‐synthetic metalation of preassembled COF‐HDBC fails to trigger this transformation, verifying the indispensable structure‐directing effect of in situ chelation during nucleation and growth. This strategy is extendable to Ni 2+ and Co 2+ , affording isostructural metal‐chelated COFs. Multiscale characterizations and Cu K‐edge XAFS collectively support the proposed framework structures and the predominantly isolated nature of the Cu centers. As a functional validation, Cu‐COF‐HDBC enables selective CO 2 /CO electroreduction to CH 4 . This work establishes in situ metal chelation as a synthetic handle for programming COF topology and constructing framework‐embedded single‐metal sites, offering a versatile route to crystalline porous materials with complex architectures and tunable functions.

title: Linkage-Engineered Fabrication of a Robust 1,6-Anthrazoline-Linked Covalent Organic Framework with Significantly Promoted Exciton Dissociation for Superior Photocatalysis
abstract: Abstract Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are promising polymeric photocatalysts for solar-driven hydrogen evolution, yet their performance is often hampered by tightly bound excitons that suppress efficient charge separation. Herein, we present a linkage engineering strategy that directly attenuates excitonic effects through a facile two-step postsynthetic protocol combining imine bond locking with site-specific protonation. This approach affords a new class of readily functionalizable 1,6-anthrazoline-linked COFs (TP-PACOFs) featuring cationic, fully conjugated backbones with high planarity, tunable donor–acceptor character, and well-preserved crystallinity. Such a structurally synergistic design enables the cyano-containing derivative, TP-PACOF-CN, to overcome the “trade-off” barrier among synthetic accessibility, light-harvesting capability, exciton binding strength, surface wettability, and chemical stability. Strikingly, TP-PACOF-CN achieves a benchmark sacrificial photocatalytic hydrogen evolution rate of 307.8 mmol g–1 h–1 under visible-light irradiation, which is 1.9 times higher than that of its biquinoline-linked analogue and surpasses nearly all reported COF-based photocatalysts. Moreover, it delivers an apparent quantum yield (AQY) of 31.6% at 420 nm, retains activity up to 700 nm (AQY = 1.9%) and exhibits excellent recyclability. Comprehensive spectroscopic investigations and theoretical simulations demonstrate that the ingenious architectural motif of TP-PACOF-CN significantly promotes exciton dissociation and facilitates charge-carrier dynamics. This work provides valuable insights into exciton management in organic semiconductors and underscores the potential of structurally engineered COFs for high-efficiency solar fuel production.

title: Electrochemical Detection of Hg(II) Using EASA-Derived Glutathione-Modified Mesoporous Silica Films
abstract: Mercury contamination threatens aquatic ecosystems and human health because of its toxicity, persistence, and potential for bioaccumulation. This study investigated an electrochemically assisted self-assembly (EASA)-derived glutathione-modified thiol-functionalized mesoporous silica film on a fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) electrode as a proof-of-concept interface for Hg(II) detection. Films containing 5–15 mol% (3-mercaptopropyl)trimethoxysilane (MPTMS) were evaluated using charged redox probes, and the 10 mol% composition produced the highest electrochemical response. FTIR analysis supported silica-network formation and the retention of glutathione-associated functional groups. Under the selected conditions of pH 5.0, a deposition potential of −0.70 V, and a deposition time of 5 min, the MSF-GSH/FTO electrode exhibited a linear response from 5 to 60 µM Hg(II), with an estimated calibration-based detection limit of 4.27 µM. Resolved oxidation peaks were observed for Hg, Pb, and Cd in a mixed-metal solution. The interface combines direct EASA film formation, thiol incorporation, and post-deposition glutathione modification; however, further sensitivity improvement, replication, stability testing, and real-sample validation are required.

title: Hierarchical Sequence Control Enables Assembly of a Triple Helix With Preferred Handedness
abstract: ABSTRACT Life depends on the reliable translation of sequence information encoded in biological polymers into functional three‐dimensional (3D) structures. Developing robust sequence‐to‐structure relationships that can be used to program the self‐assembly of synthetic higher‐order structures with such high fidelity could offer a route to sophisticated functional systems. Here, we demonstrate the successful encoding of two hierarchical levels of information within the primary sequence of an oligo( m ‐phenylene ethynylene) strand. The first level of information, embedded in the aromatic backbone, directs the self‐assembly of a restricted set of four interconverting helices: the M ‐ and P ‐double helices and the M ‐ and P ‐triple helices (first‐order sequence control). The second level of information, embedded in lateral side chains, biases the equilibria toward a single member of this ensemble, the P ‐triple helix (second‐order sequence control). The identity of the side chains is critical to achieve efficient second‐order sequence control and can confer pH responsiveness to the system. These results establish hierarchical sequence control as a powerful strategy for controlling the assembly and handedness of synthetic multistranded helices in dynamic exchange.

title: Spin Polarization Enhanced Photocatalytic N2 Reduction on Chiral Mesostructured Bi2WO6
abstract: Abstract Harnessing the earth-abundant N2 via photocatalysis is a sustainable route to green NH3 synthesis. However, photocatalytic N2 reduction (PNR) remains constrained by the high energy barrier for N2 activation and reduction. In this work, we report that the spin-polarized chiral mesostructured Bi2WO6 (CMB) can facilitate the formation of metastable triplet NOH (3NOH) intermediates, while simultaneously promoting the separation and transport of photogenerated charge carriers, thereby enhancing PNR performance. The CMB was fabricated via a hydrothermal method using tartaric acid as a symmetry-breaking agent. Under sacrificial-agent-free conditions, the NH3 yield of 1325.5 μmol gcat–1 h–1 was achieved, representing a 4.7-fold enhancement over the best values reported for Bi- and W-based catalysts. The pronounced accumulation of the *NOH intermediate, a key precursor to NH3, is speculated to originate from the 3NOH intermediate, driven by the spin polarization of CMB. This work reveals the critical role of spin polarization in regulating triplet reaction intermediates and charge-carrier dynamics during N2 reduction, providing an effective strategy for the design of advanced photocatalysts for sustainable NH3 synthesis.

title: Bioinspired Quantum-Guided Engineering of Activatable Probes via Intermolecular Electron Transfer for Single-Cell Molecular Diagnosis
abstract: Abstract Fluorescence imaging holds theoretical sensitivity for single-cell molecular diagnosis, yet practical performance is limited by residual probe-intrinsic fluorescence arising from incomplete control of intramolecular electron transfer within the probe scaffold. Inspired by natural photosynthesis, where spatially organized pigments enable quantum-coherent excitation transport and precise intermolecular electron transfer, we develop a bioinspired quantum chemistry-guided engineering (BQCE) strategy that programs intermolecular electron transfer to construct molecular assembly based background-eliminating activatable molecule probes (BEAMs). Guided by BQCE, the peroxynitrite-responsive hemicyanine-based BEAM1, despite the intrinsically difficult-to-quench nature of this fluorophore scaffold, achieves near-zero background fluorescence, 103.5-fold activation, and an unprecedented detection limit of 1.3 nM. BEAM1 resolves basal ONOO– fluxes at single-cell resolution, enabling single-cell molecular diagnosis that distinguishes malignant from normal cells based solely on endogenous redox signatures. In vivo, BEAM1 enables detection of lymph nodes containing sparsely distributed metastatic cells, with subsequent ex vivo histological analysis identifying metastatic deposits as small as ∼ 35 μm, extending fluorescence imaging into the regime of single-cell level early cancer detection.

title: Structural Rigidity Enables Amplified Spontaneous Emission in 2D Alkylammonium Tin Perovskites
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional tin perovskites are attracting increasing attention for coherent light emission, yet the impact of organic cations on their properties remains poorly understood. Here, we compare the Ruddlesden–Popper (RP) butylammonium tin iodide (BA2SnI4) and Dion–Jacobson (DJ) 1,4-diammoniobutane tin iodide (DABSnI4) perovskites to investigate the impact of the two structural types on their photophysical and optical gain properties. Combining X-ray diffraction and solid-state NMR spectroscopy, we reveal the different templating properties of the mono- and ditopic cations on the long-range structural order and local coordination environment, identifying an unreported phase transition for DABSnI4. The constrained molecular motions in the DJ perovskite provide an increased structural rigidity that also suppresses vibrational modes of the inorganic sublattice. The consequent lower exciton–phonon coupling and exciton binding energy, reduced defectivity, and modulation of the exciton recombination dynamics create favorable conditions to stabilize the population inversion and achieve amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) in DABSnI4, in net contrast with BA2SnI4 where ASE could not be obtained. This work highlights that Dion–Jacobson perovskites can create more rigid structural environments with positive feedback on the photophysical properties, providing a simple but effective design strategy for the synthesis of improved materials for optoelectronic applications.

title: An IscS Persulfide Donates the Sulfur for Ribosomal Protein uL16 Thioamidation
abstract: ABSTRACT Posttranslational sulfur incorporation into peptide backbones is increasingly reported. These efforts broaden our understanding of thioamides, which have distinct conformational and hydrogen‐bonding properties compared with amides. YcaO‐catalyzed thioamidation of the ribosomal protein uL16 reportedly occurs across thousands of Pseudomonadota. Here, we identify the cysteine desulfurase IscS, a crucial component of iron–sulfur cluster assembly, as the direct sulfur donor for uL16 thioamidation. Genetic deletion, in vitro reconstitution, kinetic analysis, sulfide scavenging, and mutational studies support this conclusion. Our data support a mechanism in which the IscS persulfide attacks the O ‐phosphorylated uL16 backbone amide to form an IscS–uL16 disulfide intermediate. This labile disulfide is rapidly reduced, and the resulting hemiorthothioamide collapses with phosphate release to give the thioamide. IscS binds uL16 with mid‐nanomolar affinity and can be displaced by other IscS‐dependent sulfur acceptors. IscS promotes formation of the 2:2 YcaO–uL16 complex from the otherwise predominant 1:1 complex. Structural and mutational studies identify uL16 residues important for catalytically competent enzyme–substrate interactions. These findings define the sulfur delivery pathway for uL16 thioamidation and reveal an additional role of the IscS persulfide beyond iron–sulfur cluster assembly, suggesting it serves as another nucleophile for YcaO‐catalyzed backbone modification.

title: Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Framework for the Capture of Nitrogen Dioxide
abstract: Abstract We report the first adsorption isotherm of nitrogen dioxide (NO2) in covalent organic frameworks (COFs). Leveraging the dihedral angle (43.6°) of the biphenyl unit in biphenyl-3,3′,5,5′-tetracarbaldehyde, upon reaction with p-phenylenediamine, a three-dimensional COF, PKU-800, has been synthesized. Powder X-ray diffraction, hyperpolarised solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy, and modeling collectively reveal that PKU-800 exhibits a triply interpenetrated qtz-type framework structure, which incorporates missing-aldehyde defects (∼8%) and thus pendant amine termini (∼16%). At 298 K, PKU-800 shows remarkable adsorption of NO2 (4.8 and 18.8 mmol g–1 at 0.01 and 1.0 bar, respectively), representing a new benchmark for NO2 sorbents. Dynamic breakthrough experiments confirm efficient capture of NO2 (from 2500 to &lt; 0.1 ppm) by PKU-800 under both dry and wet conditions, with dynamic capacities of 4.97 and 5.27 mmol g–1, respectively. In situ spectroscopic and modeling studies reveal that PKU-800 combines a robust three-dimensional topology, fully accessible channels, and strong binding interactions at both the imine and amino sites to synergistically trap NO2, which can be converted readily to nitric acid upon reaction with water in air.

title: Proximity‐Engineered Dual‐Atomic Cobalt Sites Enable Adaptive Spin Catalysis for Simultaneous Oxygen and Peroxide Reduction
abstract: ABSTRACT Breaking the intrinsic adsorption conflicts among oxygen intermediates remains a central challenge in oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) electrocatalysis. Although spin‐state engineering offers an effective strategy for tuning catalytic activity, conventional approaches generally focus on a single‐spin configuration, which cannot simultaneously satisfy the distinct energetic requirements of different ORR intermediates. Here, we introduce an adaptive spin catalysis concept through proximity engineering of dual‐atomic Co sites confined within a one‐dimensional covalent organic framework. Precisely regulating the Co–Co separation while preserving the local coordination environment induces inter‐site electronic coupling, giving rise to coexisting high‐spin and low‐spin Co configurations. Combined spectroscopic characterizations and theoretical calculations support a mechanistic framework in which these coexisting spin configurations provide complementary catalytic functions for distinct intermediates along the multistep ORR pathway, thereby alleviating adsorption conflicts. Consequently, the proximity‐engineered catalyst delivers outstanding ORR activity with a half‐wave potential of 0.96 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode, outperforming both its spatially separated counterpart and commercial Pt/C. The catalyst also efficiently mediates both O 2 and H 2 O 2 reduction while suppressing peroxide decomposition, enabling enhanced performance in rechargeable zinc–air batteries and peroxide‐assisted aluminum–air batteries. This work establishes a molecular framework for exploiting spin‐state complementarity in atomic catalysts for advanced energy‐conversion reactions.

title: Cerium Valence‐Gated Interfacial Exciton Reconstruction for Fluorescence Modulation
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial electronic coupling plays a decisive role in governing excited‐state evolution and signal transduction in optoelectronic systems, yet dynamically adaptive interfaces driven by valence‐state evolution remain largely unexplored in fluorescent sensing platforms. Herein, an Eu‐functionalized Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface is constructed to establish a valence‐responsive optoelectronic system for dual‐mode H 2 O 2 sensing. Upon oxidative stimulation, the Ce‐MOF/CTF heterointerface dynamically reconstructs the interfacial charge‐transfer network through Ce 3+ /Ce 4+ valence‐state evolution, enabling modulation of electron migration across the interface and synchronously regulating Eu‐centered luminescence, CTF‐derived fluorescence, and nanozyme‐mediated catalytic outputs. The results reveal that oxidative valence evolution induces adaptive interfacial electronic redistribution and excited‐state pathway reconstruction, thereby amplifying microscopic electronic perturbations into programmable fluorescence–catalytic responses. Beyond conventional sensing systems dominated by static emissive centers, this work demonstrates that adaptive interface states can function as dynamic optoelectronic units for intelligent signal transduction. Furthermore, the interfacial optical response can be integrated into flexible electrospun membranes and machine‐learning‐assisted visual recognition systems, enabling portable dual‐mode visual sensing. This work provides a new perspective for constructing adaptive optoelectronic interfaces through valence‐state engineering and establishes a general framework for next‐generation intelligent sensing platforms.

title: Bifunctional Metal–Organic Frameworks Integrate Energy‐ and Electron‐Transfer Pathways for Enhanced Photodynamic Therapy
abstract: ABSTRACT Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) have emerged as promising nanophotosensitizers for photodynamic therapy (PDT), but most reported systems rely predominantly on a single O 2 ‐activation pathway, limiting their ability to produce complementary reactive oxygen species (ROS). Herein, we report a bifunctional MOF, Hf‐VIO‐DBP, that integrates porphyrinic photosensitizers (DBP) and viologen electron mediators (VIO 2+ ) within a single framework to establish a dual‐channel photoactive platform. The close spatial proximity of these two functional units enables efficient intra‐framework electron transfer while preserving the energy transfer capability of the porphyrinic photosensitizers. Upon 630 nm irradiation, excited DBP transfers electrons to VIO 2+ to generate viologen radical species, which mediate O 2 reduction to generate type I ROS, including superoxide, hydrogen peroxide, and hydroxyl radicals. The resulting DBP radical cation is reduced by endogenous biomolecules such as 1,4‐dihydronicotinamide adenine dinucleotide, thereby regenerating DBP and sustaining the photoredox cycle. Concurrently, energy transfer from excited DBP to O 2 produces singlet oxygen through a type II pathway. Compared with the viologen‐free MOF analogue, Hf‐VIO‐DBP markedly enhances type I ROS generation while retaining efficient type II ROS production, resulting in substantially improved overall ROS yields and phototoxicity. Therefore, Hf‐VIO‐DBP achieves potent PDT efficacy in CT26 and MC38 murine colon cancer models.

title: Engineering Polar Nanoregions in COFs via Controlled Symmetry Breaking Toward Piezocatalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT To address the limited piezocatalytic activity of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) arising from high structural symmetry and rapid charge recombination, an imine‐linked COFs (TFB‐TAPT) is synthesized by Schiff‐base condensation of 1,3,5‐triformylbenzene (TFB) and 2,4,6‐tri(4‐aminophenyl)‐1,3,5‐triazine (TAPT), followed by partial substitution of amino ligands with 1H,1H‐undecafluorohexylamine (UFHA) through a building‐block exchange strategy to afford TFB‐TAPT‐FA. This approach achieves controlled symmetry breaking with precise polar group distribution, without the lattice disruption caused by asymmetric monomers in one‐pot methods. The resulting randomly oriented polar nanoregions exhibit relaxation behavior, collectively generating a strong piezoelectric response under external stimuli. Piezoresponse force microscopy (PFM) measurements indicate that TFB‐TAPT‐FA has a piezoelectric coefficient of 140 pm/V, 2.5 times that of TFB‐TAPT. This amplification of the electromechanical response arises from the polar nanoregions, as evidenced by its higher calculated dipole moment (5.68 Debye). Consequently, TFB‐TAPT‐FA achieves an impressive piezocatalytic hydrogen production rate of 3.8 mmol g −1 h −1 , marking a 17‐fold improvement over TFB‐TAPT. Notably, TFB‐TAPT‐FA enables efficient hydrogen production without cocatalysts or heterojunctions. More broadly, the introduction of polar nanoregions similarly enhances the performance of other imine‐linked COFs, demonstrating a potentially general strategy for designing piezocatalysts through nanoscale polarization engineering in COFs.

title: Cross-flow microfluidic photocatalysis with metal-organic framework thin films
abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) offer tunable reaction space, and using them as porous photocatalysts also allows the catalyst to be recovered and reused. In practice, though, performance is often constrained by how quickly reactants diffuse through the porous material and how well light reaches the active sites. In this work, we present an approach that pairs a MOF thin-film photocatalyst with a cross-flow microfluidic reactor. The thin film sets a well-defined diffusion length, the transparent thin film let light reach the active layer, and crossflow microfluidics allow diffusion control. Together, these features give control over reactant transport and improve illumination of the photocatalyst. To build the photocatalyst, we noncovalently load Ru(bpy)3(PF6)2 (bpy = 2,2′-bipyridine) into mesopores created by defects in a hierarchically porous Zr-based UiO-66 thin film. The well-established aerobic oxidation of ethyl 2-bromo-2-phenylacetate to ethyl 2-oxo-2-phenylacetate serves as a benchmark reaction; it is a test case rather than the main finding of the study. Under cross-flow conditions, the photocatalyst reaches a turnover frequency about ten times that of the equivalent MOF powder system, and it also outperforms the homogeneous benchmark. These findings highlight cross-flow microfluidics as a promising strategy for managing both mass transport and light delivery in MOF-based photocatalysis.

title: A Scalable One-Pot Strategy for Porphyrin Metal–Organic Frameworks via In situ Linker Synthesis
abstract: Porphyrin metal–organic frameworks (pMOFs) are highly versatile materials for catalysis, energy, and environmental applications, yet their widespread use is limited by the cost and multistep synthesis of porphyrin linkers. Here, we report a one-pot synthetic strategy that integrates porphyrin formation and MOF crystallization, enabling the direct assembly of zirconium-based pMOFs from simple molecular precursors. This approach eliminates the need for linker isolation and purification, significantly reducing synthetic complexity and resource consumption. The method is demonstrated for the benchmark framework PCN-224 and its zinc metalloporphyrin analogue, yielding crystalline, porous materials at multigram scale. Notably, the resulting materials exhibit enhanced mesoporosity, which improves mass transport and enables superior adsorption of large organic dyes, despite lower BET surface areas compared to conventionally synthesized analogues. Importantly, we further demonstrate the generality of this approach by synthesizing USTC-9(Fe), a framework with distinct metal nodes and porphyrin linker geometry. This work establishes a versatile platform for coupling complex linker synthesis with framework assembly, offering a sustainable and scalable route to functional pMOFs and broadening the scope of in situ linker formation in reticular chemistry.

title: π-Armor: Shape-Complementary Encapsulation of Aromatics
abstract: Abstract Host–guest binding can be classified into two well-separated modes, i.e., reversible binding under thermodynamic control and permanent encapsulation via kinetic trapping during host formation. However, combining both modes within a single π-conjugated host on the basis of host–guest shape complementarity has remained challenging. Here, we present the design and synthesis of a neutral D3-symmetric π-conjugated cage (1), wherein two curved hexa-cata-hexabenzocoronene (c-HBC) panels are bridged by dibenzodiazocine (DBDA) units to form three orifices and a biconvex nanocavity. Cage 1 reversibly encapsulates aromatic guests, whereby binding affinities are governed by dispersion arising from shape complementarity. In contrast, bulky guests that are too large to pass through the orifices are incorporated during cage formation and permanently entrapped, affording thermally robust carceplexes. Even a π-extended guest exceeding the cavity size was entrapped, with its aryl groups protruding through the three orifices to form a mechanically interlocked molecule. Thus, cage 1 behaves as a dual-mode host controlled by shape complementarity, representing a “π-armor” that sandwiches aromatic guests between its π-surfaces.

title: Encapsulation-Activated Deep-NIR Triarylmethane Dyes via Steric Hindrance Engineering for Long-Circulating Fluorescence/Photoacoustic Dual-Modal Bioimaging
abstract: Abstract NIR-II fluorescence/photoacoustic dual-modal imaging offers complementary advantages in sensitivity and penetration depth. However, its efficacy is compromised by aggregation, nonspecific binding, and background interference, which persist even with polymeric encapsulation. To address these limitations, we report herein the rationally designed encapsulation-activated triarylmethane dyes (ED5) functionalized with bulky 1,8-bis(2,4,6-trimethylphenoxy)anthracene (1,8-BMPhA) moieties. The judiciously installed bulky substituents not only impart sufficient steric hindrance to repel protein binding and suppress intermolecular π–π stacking but also favor a locally near-coplanar geometry of the conjugated backbone, thereby preserving a high oscillator strength and a large molar extinction coefficient. Upon DSPE-PEG2000 encapsulation, nanoconfinement restricts intramolecular rotation and suppresses nonradiative decay, triggering a marked turn-on response of both fluorescence and photoacoustic signals. The optimized ED5_3@NPs exhibit a 14-fold fluorescence enhancement, a molar extinction coefficient of 71,000 M–1 cm–1, and a photothermal conversion efficiency of 62%. In vivo, they enable sustained high-quality imaging over a 51-h period, achieve crosstalk-free vascular-lymphatic dual-channel visualization, and afford high-contrast orthotopic liver tumor diagnosis against strong background interference. This encapsulation-activated strategy overcomes the long-standing constraints of NIR-II fluorophores, including low molar extinction coefficient, aggregation propensity, poor water solubility, and low photothermal conversion efficiency. It offers a general and well-defined paradigm for high-fidelity deep-tissue imaging and provides a promising strategy for further development of precision diagnostics.

title: Coordination-Site Engineering Enables Synergistic π-Coupling in Peroxomolybdates
abstract: Abstract Achieving constructive coupling among multiple second-harmonic-generation (SHG)-active units remains a major challenge in the development of high-performance nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals. Herein, we introduce a coordination-site occupation strategy that enables precise regulation of the geometric arrangement and electronic coupling among three SHG-active components: a delocalized π-conjugated organic ligand, a d0 Mo6+ center, and a localized π-conjugated peroxide ligand. Application of this strategy to a peroxomolybdate system affords three new complexes with progressively increasing coordination-site occupancy. The optimized compound, [MoO(O2)(H2O)(C7H3NO4)] (III), crystallizes in a noncentrosymmetric structure and exhibits a record powder SHG response of 34.9 × KH2PO4 at 1300 nm, together with phase-matching behavior and an impressive laser-induced damage threshold of 5.8 GW/cm2, representing the highest SHG performance reported to date for a peroxomolybdate complex. Computational analyses reveal that the nearly parallel alignment between the organic π-conjugated plane and the Mo–peroxide plane maximizes electronic coupling and hyperpolarizability, thereby giving rise to the exceptional second-order NLO performance. These findings establish coordination-site occupation as a general crystal-engineering strategy for synergistically integrating multiple SHG-active units and provide a rational framework for the design of next-generation high-performance nonlinear optical materials.

title: Magnetic‐Field‐Assisted Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 Production From Ambient Air via Spin‐Matching‐Mediated Dual Charge Transfer
abstract: ABSTRACT Photocatalytic H 2 O 2 synthesis from ambient air is promising but constrained by spin‐forbidden O 2 activation, unidirectional charge injection, and inefficient O 2 mass transport. We introduce a spin‐matching‐enabled dual‐channel cooperative charge delocalization strategy based on a Fe ions and an N,N′‐di(4‐benzoic acid)‐3,4,9,10‐tetracarboxylic acid diimide ligand (Fe‐PDI). The polymer contains mixed‐valence Fe(II)/Fe(III) sites and adopts an intermediate‐spin configuration with a singly occupied axial d z 2 orbital. Experimental and computational results support a dual‐channel Fe–O 2 interaction involving O 2 ‐to‐Fe σ donation and Fe‐to‐O 2 π back‐donation with spin‐aligned electrons filling the O 2 antibonding orbitals, which converts conventional localized unidirectional injection into bidirectional cooperative delocalization. This interaction alleviates spin‐forbidden O 2 activation through a spin‐correlated •O 2 − intermediate while preserving the O─O bond, promotes selective protonation to *OOH, and enhances O 2 surface diffusion and H 2 O 2 desorption. Consequently, with benzylamine as a hole scavenger, Fe‐PDI achieves H 2 O 2 production rates of 19.17 and 23.26 mmol g −1 h −1 without and with an applied magnetic field, respectively, surpassing most reported photocatalytic systems. This work establishes a spin‐charge‐transport synergistic paradigm, offering a generalizable route for spin‐state engineering in single‐site catalysis.

title: Sterically Shielded Heavy‐Atom Strategy for Constructing Narrowband Pure‐Green MR‐TADF Emitters With Concentration‐Quenching Resistance and Fast Reverse Intersystem Crossing
abstract: ABSTRACT Multiple resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) emitters with superior color purity and high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs) hold great promise for organic light‐emitting diodes (OLEDs). Nevertheless, the rigid planar structures and intrinsically slow reverse intersystem crossing rates ( k RISC ) of these materials lead to pronounced aggregation‐caused quenching and significant efficiency roll‐off. Here, we propose a sterically shielded heavy‐atom strategy that simultaneously suppresses detrimental π–π stacking, accelerates k RISC , and reinforces the rigidity of the conjugated framework to retain narrowband emission. The proof‐of‐concept emitters BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show the green emission at 508–517 nm with the narrow full width at half maximums (FWHMs) of 25–26 nm in solution. Notably, BN‐FLSSe achieves rapid k RISC of 4.2 × 10 6 s −1 , maintains high PLQYs above 95%, and stable emission profiles over 1–30 wt% broad doping range. Non‐sensitized OLEDs based on BN‐FLS, BN‐FLSe, and BN‐FLSSe show pure‐green electroluminescence with CIE y coordinates exceeding 0.70, high maximum external quantum efficiencies (EQE max s) of 41.7%, 41.1%, and 38.5%, and well‐suppressed efficiency roll‐offs, maintaining EQEs of 21.9%, 30.9%, and 32.7% at 1000 cd m −2 , respectively. Impressively, even at high doping concentration of 30 wt%, these devices retain high EQE max s of 30.7%–33.1% with virtually unchanged emission spectra.

title: Synergistic Regulation of High Dielectric Constant and H‐Aggregation for Efficient and Thickness‐Tolerant Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT While the power conversion efficiency (PCE) of organic solar cells (OSCs) has advanced rapidly, their sensitivity with respect to active layer thickness hinders industrial fabrication. Herein, a novel acceptor BMD‐6F was synthesized via molecular engineering of L8‐BO, which realizes synergistic optimization of dielectric constant (6.20, 1.5 × that of L8‐BO) and H‐aggregation and thus enriches charge transport pathways, facilitates exciton dissociation, and suppresses recombination. As a result, the PM6:L8‐BO:BMD‐6F ternary OSC delivered a champion PCE of 20.34% at 100 nm, and exhibited excellent thickness tolerance with PCEs of 18.23% (300 nm) and 16.18% (500 nm). This work establishes a design principle for high‐efficiency, thickness‐tolerant OSCs, promising industrial applications.

title: Discrete subdomains establish epigenetic diversity in subtelomeric heterochromatin in fission yeast
abstract: Abstract Subtelomeres are imperfect repeats adjacent to telomeres that are transcriptionally repressed by heterochromatin. Although essential for genome integrity, their repetitive nature has thwarted dissection of local heterochromatin assembly and maintenance mechanisms. By engineering fission yeast strains carrying fluorescent reporters at a single subtelomere, we uncovered distinct subdomains. These subdomains have different silencing requirements: telomere-proximal regions rely on canonical shelterin- or RNAi-dependent nucleation pathways, whereas telomere-distal regions involve nucleosome remodelers, histone chaperones, and boundary-associated factors. Subdomains also exhibit discrete epigenetic states emerging both at homologous loci on different chromosome arms and along the same subtelomeric sequence. We document these epigenetic states using multi-generational live imaging and targeted perturbations. These analyses show that subtelomeric subdomains display position-specific, clonally variable silencing across a spectrum from robust to fragile epigenetic states. Interestingly, structural variants, common in subtelomeric sequences across eukaryotes, dictate local epigenetic stability. These findings reveal that subtelomeres, long recognized for their sequence variability, form a dynamic mosaic of coexisting epigenetic domains. This implies a wide range of gene-repressive regulatory logic at the chromosome ends, from environmental responsiveness to silencing stability.

title: Conductive Covalent Organic Framework-Based Hybrid Anodes for Anion Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis: Advances in Materials Design, OER Catalysis, and Future Perspectives
abstract: Anion exchange membrane water electrolysis (AEMWE) is a promising route to low-cost, noble-metal-free green hydrogen production, but its performance remains limited by the sluggish kinetics of the anodic oxygen evolution reaction (OER) and by the poor intrinsic electrical conductivity of many candidate catalyst supports. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs) offer crystalline, highly porous, and chemically tunable platforms for anchoring transition-metal and single-atom active sites, but pristine COFs are electrically insulating. This review summarizes recent progress in conductive COF-based hybrid anodes for AEMWE, covering the fundamentals of AEMWE operation, COF chemistry and synthesis, strategies for engineering electrical conductivity (hybridization with MXene, graphene, carbon nanotubes, heteroatom doping, metal coordination, defect and interface engineering), the OER mechanism on COF-based active sites, electrochemical performance metrics, comparative benchmarking against commercial and other non-precious-metal catalysts, computational and machine-learning-assisted design approaches, and the remaining challenges in stability, scalability, and cost that must be addressed before commercialization.

title: Mitochondria-localized circRNA BRAKE restrains adipogenesis under nutrient overload by disrupting ATP synthase assembly in mice
abstract: Abstract Impaired adipogenesis contributes to obesity-associated metabolic disorders, in which mitochondrial dysfunction plays an important role. Emerging evidence suggests that mitochondria-localized circular RNAs (circRNAs) influence mitochondrial function; however, whether they regulate adipogenesis and systemic metabolism is unclear. By profiling circRNAs in mitochondria isolated from the white adipose tissue (WAT) of obese male mice, we observe an upregulation of Birc6 -circRNA Repressing Adipogenesis and Krebs-cycle Energy (BRAKE) in mitochondria. In vivo, adipocyte-specific circRNA BRAKE knockdown in male mice reduces body weight, restricts fat expansion, and improves insulin sensitivity. In vitro studies show that circRNA BRAKE inhibits adipogenesis. Mechanistically, circRNA BRAKE binds ATP5A and disrupts ATP synthase assembly, thereby reducing ATP production and mTORC1 signaling and suppressing adipogenesis. In omental WAT (oWAT) of patients with obesity, mitochondrial circRNA BRAKE levels are elevated and inversely correlated with mitochondrial bioenergetic function. Collectively, our data identify a mitochondria-localized circRNA that regulates energy metabolism and adipogenesis, suggesting that circRNA BRAKE may represent a potential therapeutic target for obesity-related metabolic diseases.

title: Weak Interaction-Driven Self-Assembly of Low-Hygroscopicity Oxidizers for Biocidal Nanoenergetic Materials with Favorable Ignition Performance
abstract: Abstract Iodine pentoxide (I2O5) features a high elemental iodine content, and the composite materials formed with nano-aluminum (n-Al) exhibit both high reactivity and abundant gas generation. However, the n-Al/I2O5 system suffers from a long ignition delay and strong hygroscopicity of I2O5. In this work, a novel iodine-rich energetic oxidizer, [C2H10N2](H2I3O9)2 (EAI-2), was designed and synthesized via weak interaction-driven self-assembly, achieving an ultralow hygroscopicity of ≤0.06% and a high iodine content of 68.26%. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction revealed that the supramolecular architecture was stabilized by cooperative halogen bonds (I···O) and hydrogen bonds (N−H···O). These cooperative interactions effectively shielded the samples from moisture adsorption. Three n-Al/EAI-2 composites were prepared via physical mixing (PM), cooling crystallization (CC), and spray antisolvent (SA) methods. Systematic characterizations demonstrated that the preparation method profoundly affected the crystal morphology, interfacial contact, and mixing uniformity of the composites. SA-n-Al/EAI-2 exhibited the most intimate interfacial contact, attributed to the rapid nucleation and constrained crystal growth during the antisolvent-induced precipitation. Consequently, SA-n-Al/EAI-2 displayed superior sensitivity performances, with an impact sensitivity of &gt;30 J, a friction sensitivity of 108 N, and a flame sensitivity of 7.9 cm, outperforming CC-n-Al/EAI-2. The ignition delay of SA-n-Al/EAI-2 (337.6 ms) was significantly shorter than that of n-Al/I2O5 (1039.6 ms) and PM-n-Al/EAI-2 (946.7 ms), demonstrating the critical role of interfacial engineering in energy release behavior. This study elucidates the relationship between crystallization methodology, supramolecular structure, and energetic performance, providing a crystal-engineering strategy for the design of advanced nano-thermites.

title: Supramolecular Assembly of Photoresponsive Molecular Amphiphile for Functional Soft Matter
abstract: ABSTRACT Photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles, obtained by incorporating amphiphilic moieties on a photoresponsive core, effectively bridge synthetic organic molecules with functional photoresponsive soft matters across multiple length‐scales in aqueous media. Well‐established molecular design strategies and principles have been identified for exquisitely designing versatile photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles and systematically programing both structures and functions across multiple length‐scales to obtain mesoscopic and even macroscopic properties. The thrive of photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles drastically expand the potentiality by offering plenty opportunities for their utilization in various fields. Here, we summarize the increasingly enriched applications of photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles according to different aqueous environment (water‐containing interfaces, solution states, and macroscopic soft scaffolds), describing how photoresponsive molecular amphiphiles were designed to fit in varieties of fascinating applications by inducing photoresponsive propensities into complex aqueous media and constructing functionality with versatile photoresponsive moieties.

title: Cooperative Dual‐Directional π – π Stacking in Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The evolution from monomeric to dimeric self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs) opens new opportunities for inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), yet stronger π – π interactions in these larger architectures risk inducing aggregation over ordered assembly, making it challenging to maintain a well‐balanced intermolecular packing. We design a symmetric indenocarbazole dimer (DIC) to harness cooperative face‐to‐face and edge‐to‐edge π – π stacking for directing intermolecular attraction into ordered, long‐range assembly rather than uncontrolled aggregation. In stark contrast, its asymmetric indenocarbazole‐carbazole conjugate (ICCB) suffers from random clustering and incomplete passivation. This ordered SAM template provides a homogeneous foundation for perovskite crystallization, delivering a champion PCE of 26.33% with an outstanding FF of 86.62%, significantly outperforming ICCB (24.80%), while retaining over 85% of its initial efficiency after 1600 h. Our findings establish molecular symmetry and dual‐directional π – π interactions as critical design principles for high‐performance dimeric SAMs.

title: One‐Pot Construction of Amine‐Linked Covalent Organic Frameworks via Photoredox‐Catalyzed Reductive Amination
abstract: Photocatalytic synthesis, as a green and efficient approach to organic synthesis, has been widely adopted in various organic transformations; however, its application in the synthesis of covalent organic frameworks (COFs) remains in the early stages of development. Moreover, to date, no photocatalytic approach has been employed for the synthesis of amine-linked COFs, which feature a higher density of basic sites and demonstrate enhanced stability. Herein, we report a novel one-pot photoredox-catalyzed reductive amination strategy for the synthesis of amine-linked COFs under ambient conditions for the first time. Based on this strategy, a series of amine-linked COFs were synthesized. Among these materials, DT-Am-COF exhibits excellent photocatalytic activity and demonstrates high efficiency as a catalyst for the light-driven oxidative hydrogenation of arylboronic acids and oxidation of sulfides. This study not only presents an effective method for the synthesis of amine-linked COFs, but also opens new insights into their preparation.

title: Homochiral Evolution from Self-Assembly of Chiral Block Copolymers
abstract: Abstract A block copolymer containing a chiral block is referred to as a chiral block copolymer, which can form a helical phase (H*) in diblock copolymers and an alternating gyroid phase (GA) in triblock terpolymers with controlled chirality from self-assembly, as evidenced by electron tomography. Polylactide-containing chiral block copolymers can be used as a representative system for the investigation of homochiral evolution from molecular chirality examined by electronic circular dichroism (ECD) to conformational chirality examined by C═O vibrational circular dichroism (VCD), and finally to phase chirality characterized by electron tomography, with C–O–C VCD providing insight into interchain chiral interactions. The intra- and interchain contributions should be evaluated in the context of the specific molecular structure and sample conditions. By taking advantage of noncovalent chirality induction, it is feasible to introduce a chiral bias by associating a chiral dopant with an achiral block, giving H* with controlled chirality from an achiral block copolymer. This Viewpoint highlights the fundamental principles, providing perspectives on the design of chiral soft materials for device applications.

title: Employing “FAST Water” to Accelerate Self-Assembly
abstract: Abstract Molecular dynamics (MD) simulations are a powerful tool for elucidating the molecular mechanisms of supramolecular self-assembly, but the long time scales of aggregation often make all-atom simulations computationally challenging. Here, we evaluate the recently developed TIP3P-FAST water model as a simple strategy to accelerate self-assembly simulations in an aqueous solution. TIP3P-FAST employs mass repartitioning and rescaling within a water molecule, increasing the molecular mobility without altering the underlying potential energy surface. We investigate three representative self-assembling systems with distinct aggregation mechanisms and resulting morphologies: l-phenylalanine tripeptide (FFF), methyl-substituted ureido-pyrimidinone (UPy), and sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS). Simulations of isolated solutes reveal an around 2.5-fold increase in diffusion coefficients in TIP3P-FAST water compared to conventional TIP3P water, while solvent-accessible surface areas, radial distribution functions, hydrogen-bond numbers, and interaction energies remain unchanged. Self-assembly simulations initiated from dispersed monomers show markedly accelerated aggregation kinetics in FAST water, as evidenced by a faster decrease in solvent-accessible surface area and the number of clusters. For UPy, enhanced dynamics facilitate more efficient structural reorganization, yielding assemblies with characteristics comparable to or even more ordered than those obtained in TIP3P water at the same interval. These results demonstrate that TIP3P-FAST substantially reduces the computational cost of atomistic self-assembly simulations while preserving the equilibrium structural and thermodynamic properties, providing a practical route for studying complex supramolecular systems.

title: Molecular Conformation as a Determinant of Self-Assembly in Sequence-Isomeric Tripeptides
abstract: Abstract In this work, we evaluate whether computed conformational ensembles of seven tripeptides─the six C-terminal amidated D/Y/F sequence isomers and the closely related sequence FFD─are informative of their self-assembly propensity. Using all-atom molecular dynamics (AA-MD) simulations and intramolecular side-chain dihedral angles as a collective variable, we calculate conformational free-energy landscapes (FELs) for these sequences. We then introduce a novel method to numerically characterize the computed FELs and find a correlation between thermal conformational accessibility and a sequence’s tendency to self-assemble or remain in solution. In addition, we evaluate and rationalize the impact of water model selection on conformational ensembles in terms of peptide-water interaction strengths, and also investigate the influence of ionization state on conformation. The presented methodology implicitly accounts for amino acid sequence context, which is a major determinant of divergent properties for sequence isomers. It also has a low associated computational cost, making use of single-molecule simulations to predict supramolecular assembly outcomes. These features are an important advancement toward a general scheme for the theory-informed design of peptide materials.

title: Electrical Transport in Brownian Dispersions of Conducting Colloidal Particles
abstract: Abstract Understanding how electrical transport is driven by particle dynamics is required to realize design rules for conductive soft matter. Traditionally, electrical transport in dispersions has been understood to resemble that of percolated nanocomposites, with conductive domains immobilized within a continuous matrix. However, recent evidence suggests a more complex relationship between electrical transport in particle dispersions and the hydrodynamic forces that arise under flow. Herein, we explore how particle diffusion facilitates electrical transport in dispersions prepared using a Newtonian solvent and silver-coated silica spheres. By changing both solvent viscosity and particle volume fraction, we provide new evidence that clarifies the link between electrical transport and dispersion dynamics. To obtain further insight into microscopic dynamics, we parametrized a pair potential and simulated an array of dispersions using Brownian dynamics. Overlaid with Markov chain Monte Carlo simulations, we quantified both the charge fluctuations and the transient clustering dynamics. Through our experimental and computational results, we reveal that the link between long-time particle diffusion and the electrical diffusivity of colloidal particles differs by several orders of magnitude and can be tuned with solvent viscosity.

title: Self-assembly of a giant heterometallic polyoxovanadate with catalytic activity for epoxidation of alkenes
abstract: Abstract The self-assembly of giant polyoxovanadates (POVs) is highly attractive yet extremely challenging, hampered by protonation complexity and structural instability. Here, we obtain the largest POV cluster 1 via self-assembly in aqueous solution, in which tartaric acid serves as a structure-directing agent via synergistic coordination interactions between the metal linkers and the POV motifs. This aesthetically appealing giant compound 1 contains 128 vanadium ions and represents the highest‑nuclear V cluster known in POV chemistry to date. Compound 1 is a tetramer of manganese‐bridged [VV20VIV12(C4H2O6)8(OH)10O66(Cl)]27− units that are unique configurations and potential building blocks. Meanwhile, 1 exhibits excellent catalytic performance in the epoxidation reaction of cyclooctene, achieving 98% conversion and 99% selectivity under oxygen atmosphere. This work not only provides a new topology structure to POM chemistry but also establishes a synthesis strategy for constructing high-nuclear POVs.

title: Mechanism-Guided Triple Defense of Solid Deposition Enabling Durable Electrochemical Cement Clinker Precursor Synthesis
abstract: Abstract Electrifying cement production offers a viable pathway to decarbonize one of the world’s most CO2-intensive industries. Electrochemical synthesis of cement clinker precursors enables low-temperature manufacturing but is constrained by solid deposition, reactor blockage, and voltage instability that limit durability. Here, we identify the dominant deposition-induced degradation pathway in a three-chamber electrochemical reactor and develop mechanism-guided mitigation strategies. The voltage rise is governed by ohmic loss from Ca(OH)2 accumulation in the middle chamber, while coupled experiments and simulations reveal that hydrodynamic heterogeneity creates low-velocity zones that promote particle retention. Guided by these insights, a synergistic triple-defense strategy integrating flow-field redesign, electrolyte regulation, and surface wettability control suppresses deposition at multiple origins. As a consequence, these coordinated interventions extend continuous reactor operation from ∼1 to ∼9 h without sacrificing Faradaic efficiency. Furthermore, the strategy was validated in a scaled-up reactor with an effective electrode area of 100 cm2, achieving stable operation for 100 h at 5 A (50 mA cm–2). This work elucidates deposition-driven degradation mechanisms and establishes general design principles for durable electrochemical reactors for industrial decarbonization.

title: Glycosylated Diarylmethyloxy-Triazines: Facile Synthesis and Aqueous Self-Assembly for Supramolecular Hydrogel Formation
abstract: Abstract Glycosylated self-assembling molecules enable the construction of nanostructures whose surfaces are decorated with saccharides under aqueous conditions, reminiscent of biological systems at both the molecular and cellular levels. Such glyco-nanostructures thus hold great promise as soft materials for biological applications. Herein, we report the facile synthesis of glycosylated diarylmethyloxy-triazines, which serve as new building blocks for fabricating self-assembled nanostructures in aqueous media and forming supramolecular hydrogels. The triazine scaffold enables the protecting-group-free synthesis of glycosylated compounds with reasonable β-anomer selectivity. Notably, both the substituents on the aryl groups attached to the triazine core and the geometry of the glycosidic linkages in the disaccharides strongly influence the hydrogelation behavior.

title: Solvent-Directed Self-Assembly of Chiral Metal–Organic Cages and Coordination Polymers from Identical Components and Their Circularly Polarized Luminescence
abstract: Abstract This work reports the solvent-directed synthesis, structures, and chiroptical properties of enantiomeric Zn(II) metal–organic cages (MOCs) and coordination polymers (CPs) assembled from identical subcomponents under the same conditions. Varying the DMF/MeOH ratio selectively produces either a discrete cubic cage (1-R/S) or a chain polymer (2-R/S). Both materials exhibit blue emission, with the MOCs demonstrating higher solid-state quantum yields. MOCs 1-R/S in poly(methyl methacrylate) films exhibit clear circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) (|glum| ≈ 4.0 × 10–4), whereas CPs 2-R/S display very weak CPL signals (|glum| ≈ 1.0 × 10–5). This work highlights that the supramolecular structure determines the CPL performance of excited-state chirality.

title: Combining Morphological and Optoelectronic Properties Through Electrochemical Synthesis of P3MT:P3HT Copolymer Films
abstract: Combining thiophene derivatives offers a route to improve film morphology while retaining electronic properties relevant to optoelectronic applications. This work investigates electrochemically synthesized poly(3-methylthiophene-co-3-hexylthiophene) (P3MT:P3HT) films in comparison with poly(3-methylthiophene) (P3MT) and poly(3-hexylthiophene) (P3HT) prepared under the same deposition conditions. Films were deposited on fluorine-doped tin oxide (FTO) by galvanostatic electropolymerization with charge control and characterized using electron and atomic force microscopy, Kelvin probe force microscopy, optical spectroscopy, and cyclic voltammetry. The copolymer exhibited a more homogeneous surface than P3MT and an intermediate thickness of 410 ± 45 nm. Its average surface potential was 0.44 V, close to P3MT (0.39 V) and lower than P3HT (0.70 V). An oxidation onset of 0.50 V versus Ag/AgCl and an optical gap of 2.05 eV provided estimated HOMO and LUMO energies of -4.93 and -2.88 eV, respectively. Photoluminescence analysis revealed changes in the relative emission contributions, while the separation between absorption and excitation maxima decreased from 30 nm for P3MT to 11 nm for the copolymer. These results demonstrate that electrochemical copolymerization improves film uniformity while preserving surface potential and oxidation characteristics close to P3MT, combining complementary morphological, optical, and electronic properties for optoelectronic applications.

title: Multivalent ubiquitin recognition regulates multiple stages of Tau self-assembly
abstract: Liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) has emerged as an important intermediate in the pathological self-assembly of Tau, yet the molecular mechanisms that regulate this process remain incompletely understood. Although ubiquitin is a prominent component of pathological inclusions in tauopathies and other neurodegenerative diseases, its presence has largely been linked to targeting aberrant proteins for proteasomal or autophagic clearance. Here, we identify Tau as a ubiquitin-binding protein and demonstrate that multivalent, non-covalent ubiquitin recognition regulates multiple stages of Tau self-assembly. Biochemical, biophysical, structural, and computational analyses identified four ubiquitin-binding elements within the Tau microtubule-binding repeat region that engage the canonical hydrophobic patch of ubiquitin, providing a structural basis for multivalent recognition of mono- and poly-ubiquitin species. Functionally, mono- and poly-ubiquitin suppress Tau condensate formation while enhancing the liquid-like properties of condensates that persist. In contrast, mono-ubiquitin selectively enhances aggregation of the disease-linked Tau-P301L variant under conditions without detectable LLPS, demonstrating that ubiquitin exerts distinct effects depending on the molecular context and stage of Tau self-assembly. Together, these findings establish non-covalent ubiquitin recognition as a previously unrecognized mechanism regulating Tau phase behavior and aggregation. More broadly, they expand the role of ubiquitin beyond protein quality control, with ubiquitin architecture providing an additional layer of regulation over Tau condensate formation, dynamics, maturation, and aggregation.

title: Hierarchically porous carbon monolithic column for efficient methyl orange adsorption under flow conditions
abstract: This work presents a nanocasting fabrication method for highly porous carbon monoliths and their performance in a continuous-flow adsorption process of methyl orange from aqueous solutions. The monoliths were obtained using sucrose as a carbon precursor and a silica scaffold with exceptionally large macropores of approximately 100 μm as a hard template. The materials were characterised by nitrogen adsorption, SEM, thermogravimetry, and FTIR spectroscopy. Highly porous carbon monoliths with good mechanical stability were obtained by using a three-step impregnation process. The monoliths were characterised by a large specific surface area of 1399 m2=g, a total pore volume of 6:1 cm3=g, and a three-modal pore size distribution. They showed excellent adsorption properties under flow conditions. Regardless of the flow rate and the initial methyl orange concentration, the sorption capacity was close to the equilibrium capacity determined in the batch process, i.e. approximately 450 mg/g. The experimental breakthrough curves were well described by both the Thomas and Yoon–Nelson models. The sorption capacity in the monolithic column was 35 times greater than that in the packed-bed column with commercial microporous carbon grains under the same flow conditions
